title: DR1's confirmation page tells a user who submitted an incomplete notification what they still have to do before the consignment is imported; the frontend has no such section.

finding.frontend: Below the reference panel the confirmation page shows the declaration date and then goes to 'Transporting the consignment', at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/confirmation/template.njk:4-21. There is no outstanding-items section, and nothing in the confirmation copy or controller that could produce one. The frontend does reach the state that section is for: readiness treats a task row as satisfied when it is fulfilled, not applicable or optional (src/server/app/flow/section-status.js:11-15), so a notification with no documents uploaded passes the gate. The captured Check your answers page is exactly that notification, and its user can submit with the health certificate still to come and be told nothing about it.
finding.prototype: When the notification was submitted with things still outstanding, the page opens under the panel with 'Before the consignment is imported', the line 'You still need to:' and a list of what is left — in the capture, 'upload the health certificate and any other required documents' and 'complete the animal identifier information in the notification' (app/views/notification-submitted.html:27-37). The list is built at submission time and holds only the two things DR1 lets a user submit without: documents, which are never mandatory, and animal identifiers, which are a soft follow-up once the per-species minimum is met (app/routes.js:5674-5692). Everything else DR1 treats as mandatory and refuses to submit without, so the section never carries it.
finding.difference: Record, at the moment the declaration is submitted, which optional-at-submission items were left outstanding, and render them on the confirmation page under a 'Before the consignment is imported' heading with the line 'You still need to:' above a bullet list, between the reference panel and 'Transporting the consignment'. Start with the one item the frontend can already produce — no documents uploaded — because the documents task row is optional and a notification with none of them already submits today. Add the animal-identifier item alongside whatever the identification work settles about a per-species minimum. Nothing blocks this: it needs no change to what the frontend will let a user submit.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding that DR1 renders this section on every submitted notification rather than only where something is outstanding, which would make it unconditional page furniture rather than a report on the submission.
finding.correction: The substance stands — the frontend has no outstanding-items section and DR1 does — but the finding's dependency was wrong and has been rewritten, along with the frontend slot and the related-finding relation. Claimed: that this 'depends on the frontend first allowing an incomplete notification to be submitted', scheduled after review--incomplete-notification-cannot-be-reviewed, because the frontend 'will not let a notification be submitted at all until every task row is complete, so it has no idea of a submission with items left over'. What is true: DR1 refuses Continue on its own review page while anything mandatory is outstanding (app/routes.js:10068-10075), so DR1's 'incomplete submission' is not an incomplete notification in the gating sense at all — getConditionalSubmissionItems (app/routes.js:5674-5692) builds the list from exactly two soft items, missing documents and incomplete animal identifiers, both of which DR1 permits at submission. The frontend permits the first of those today: readyForCheckYourAnswers accepts a row that is FULFILLED, NA or OPTIONAL (src/server/app/flow/section-status.js:11-15), and the captured Check your answers page is a notification with zero documents that passed the gate. So the section is buildable now, the depends-on was a false blocker that would have parked it behind a much larger flow change, and the relation is now travels-with. Confidence raised to high: both sides are observable — DR1's capture renders the section with both bullets, the frontend's renders nothing between the panel and the declaration date.

relatedTo.why: both are about how the service tells a user what is still outstanding, one before submission and one after
